utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About this exhibit, when he explained that it was signed by Martic, I believe that you cannot properly introduce an exhibit like this through this witness for several reasons. First of all, it's not his document. Second, he doesn't know. He only thinks it was signed by Martic. Third, it does not bear the stamp that belongs to the authority mentioned in the letterhead. It is the stamp of the Knin municipality. And fourth, I believe such a stamp should be procured from the competent authority. Maybe the lady on the opposite side can introduce this through another witness but not through this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we have ruled often enough and told you often enough before that as far as documents are concerned, we admit them for what they're worth. Usually their value can be seen from what's written on them. They speak for themselves. There is no hearsay rule, as you've been told often enough, in this Tribunal. Now, the points that you make as to the witness recognising the signature of Martic, the letterhead and the stamp, these are all matters of detail and you can ask the witness about them. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday we spoke about this document Mr. Milosevic referred to this morning, and it was a request by Milan Martic to Defence Minister of Serbia, Mr. Simovic, from the 18th of September, 1991. I would like to put to you now another document, and it is Exhibit 352, tab 4. It is a document from the Ministry of Defence of Serbia dated the 1st of November, 1991, and it refers to a report on assisting Serbian areas in Croatia. Looking at the letterhead and the stamp on this document, can you comment on both? Are they what you knew they looked like?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Looking at the letterhead and the stamp, I can say they were the letterhead and the stamp used in the administration of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the person signing this letter, it says Deputy Minister Major General Branislav Kuzmanovic. Do you know whether this person was at that time in this position and do you know him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He became deputy to the Minister Simovic, but I don't know his exact name. That is the Deputy Minister I met in Simovic's office. I don't know if it was Kuzmanovic at the time, but there was a person named Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this letter, General Kuzmanovic requests that the following items be put on the agenda of the government session of the Republic of Serbia, and it's reporting on assisting the Serbian areas in Croatia. Are you aware that at that time this was a point of discussion within the Serbian government?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure whether it was a topic of discussion, but I have already spoken about the way in which the competent ministers, municipality presidents, and others, sought help for Krajina in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in November 1991, did you ask for assistance, or in the month before, did the government of the SAO ask for assistance from the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beginning with September and October, yes, assistance was sought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now with the help of the usher, another document. It is tab 5 of Exhibit 352, and it's again the Ministry of Defence of Serbia, addressing, on the 1st of November, 1991, the government of the Republic of Serbia, and reports on providing assistance to the Serbian districts in Croatia. Did you have time to review this complex document while you had your conversations with the Prosecutor in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, in November 1991, and the time before, was assistance provided in the way described in paragraph 1 of this report?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistance was extended. I don't know exactly in what amount.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please have a look at attachment 5 to this report, attachment 5. Sorry, sir. Attachment 4. I made a mistake. Attachment 4. Attachment 4 is the overall assistance required for the Serb-populated areas in Croatia, and it is here the total amount is 1,2 billion dinar. Would you know how many Deutschmark that was at that time, in November 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can hardly remember the exchange rate that applied at the time. I couldn't tell you the figure in Deutschmark.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Morten Torkildsen, the expert we have in house, actually looked at the figures and found that the exchange rate, the official exchange rate with Deutschmark at that time, according to this official exchange rate, of 30 Deutschmarks -- it amounts to an official Deutschmark value of about 92 million Deutschmarks, and on the black market it was about 30 million Deutschmarks, almost 31 million Deutschmarks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now, please, look at attachment 5, and it refers to a table of the number of personnel of the TO in the SAOs. And I would like you to comment only on the figures for the SAO Krajina and not for the other SAOs. And you see here the total amount of personnel for the Knin Operational Zone with 12.000, the Lika Operational Zone with 5.800, and the Kordun and Banija zone with 20.000 staff. Is that -- would that be correct, according to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are correct, according to the plan that the main headquarters of SAO Krajina made for these formations. But I have to add that at the time, especially for the area of the Operational Zone Knin, this staff was attached to the command of the Knin Corps. But the figures are accurate, in light of the planning documents of the Main Staff of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now look at attachment 6 to this report, and I would also like you to look at the columns related to the Knin Operation Zone, the Lika Operation Zone, and the Kordun and Banija Operation Zone, and here we have actually the amounts that were necessary to pay these military staff. Can you comment on the figures for these three zones? Would they be correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you look at the calculations for the manpower in these columns, the amounts should be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the attachment -- the attachments number 1 and number 2 with the list of equipment needed in communication and in other areas, could you comment on these items? Were such items needed, would you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were our planned requirements for the Territorial Defence system of SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who made this plan for the requirements in the SAO Krajina? Who put all this equipment together when needed and when?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, beginning with October, these requirements were planned by the Main Staff of the defence force of SAO Krajina and especially the chief of the Main Staff, Colonel Kasun, Dusan Kasun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Returning to the letter -- the report, the body of the report itself, it says actually on page 2, it makes a reference as follows: "Since there are no legal grounds for this, that is providing for assistance to meet these needs is not regulated by the law, we propose that these issues be legally regulated by an appropriate decree especially in view of the fact that these needs are great and can be expected to grow and the fact that other ministries also face these problems within their respective jurisdictions." And then there follows a list of ministries. Do you know whether various ministries in the Serbian government were approached in this way, and do you know of any decree?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that other Ministers in the government of Serbia were approached to seek assistance for Krajina, but I don't know specifically about this group that was supposed to discuss this within the government of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself in -- did someone from the Krajina actually have a discussion with Mr. Simovic on these needs and these matters of financing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were discussions with General Simovic. The Prime Minister of SAO Krajina talked to him too.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, for one question I would like to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at that time when those needs arose, were you actually the head of the TO of the SAO Krajina, and is that the reason why you can comment on these matters?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As Prime Minister, I was at the head of the TO as the civilian head of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can now go back into open session again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to now put to the witness, from Exhibit 352, the document tab 6, and it is a letter from Milan Martic as the Minister of Interior of the SAO to the Ministry of Interior -- to the Ministry of Interior of Serbia and to Minister Sokolovic, dated the 10th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the letterhead, the stamp, and the signature, are these -- is this a genuine document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this letter, it actually refers to funds needed and that Minister Sokolovic should exert his influence on Minister Zebic in order to receive these amounts needed, and there is actually the amount of 38 million dinars.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, according to Mr. Torkildsen, the black market value of this amount is approximately 330.000 Deutschmarks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you comment on this letter? Is the contents correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This letter reflects the circumstances and the situation that prevailed at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were the documents I wanted to put to you in this context. Were the police and the TO incorporated into the budget of the RSK at some point in time? Yesterday you said that they were financed outside of it. Were they put into the official budget at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1992, a more stable budget began to be developed for the Republic of Serbian Krajina. As for the SAO Krajina, it had a very poor budget.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the budget of the RSK was in existence, were all the expenses of the police covered in the budget or did this payment of cash outside of the budget continue?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Payments were made in cash, and the budget of the Republic of Serbian Krajina was also subsidised from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the costs of the army covered in the RSK budget or was it paid otherwise for the costs?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The budget of the Republic of Serbian Krajina only partly covered the expenses of the army, and another part of the budget was subsidised by the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and yet for another part materiel and equipment were procured outside of the budget. Also, most of the officers in the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina was financed by the General Staff of the army of Yugoslavia directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to put to you as an example a budget, which makes it easier for us to explain the proportions, and it is Exhibit 352, tab 7. It's the budget of November 1994. Did you have time to review this document while you had your conversations with the Prosecutor in The Hague so that you are familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see budgets of this form and this one during the events?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were reports made both to the government and the Assembly about the status of the budget. I'm talking about the Assembly and government of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to have a look at actually the figures in this list stating the income of the RSK, and I would like you to comment from your knowledge of the budget of the previous years. Would you please compare the proportion of the income from taxes and from the FRY, as it is stated here? Was the income deriving from taxes higher or lower or equal in the previous years before 1994? Witness, Witness, there is a statement of income and expenditure as the second page. There is a sticker. There should be a yellow sticker. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here I see expenditures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to use only the main sheet with all the summarising figures, not the detailed lists. And you see here the amount from taxes, and you also see here the additional funds from the FRY on this list. And my question was regarding the previous budgets. What was the proportion in the earlier years, comparing the taxes -- income from taxes and the income from the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major revenues came from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean in the earlier years it was the -- what was financed by the FRY was even higher than in 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, much higher. That was the time of war and armed conflicts, where the requirements for money were greater and revenues in the Krajina were lower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at the budget on this sheet, there is a position: loans from the National Bank of RSK. The budget deficits, were they financed through loans of the National Bank of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That was one of the ways of financing the budget. Based on my information, this was mostly covered from the primary issue of the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the National Bank of RSK receive its money from?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said it was from -- it was financed from primary issues. Does that mean it was newly printed money that they received from the National Bank of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That was that kind of money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the National Bank of the RSK an independent institution?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it practically operated as a branch office of the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, in relation to the figures in dinars, Mr. Torkildsen could not find the proper figure to put into Deutschmarks because the official exchange rate was 1 dinar to 1 Deutschmark, and he couldn't find any figures in relation to the black market, so I cannot give you a proper amount in Deutschmarks. It would actually be the same amount in Deutschmarks, but only officially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could the RSK or could the SAO have existed without the support from Serbia or Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, under no circumstances it could exist. SAO Krajina and RSK were completely economically and financially dependent on Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you look at the -- actually, the next page following this page listing the income, you have the page "means of production," actually, the expenditure for what it was used. And looking at especially the figures for financing the army and financing the police, those two together, is it almost two-thirds of the entire budget?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that also your recollection of the proportions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember these proportions very well. The greater portion was always spent on these requirements. Even at the time when there was no real armed conflict, we still had a state of an imminent threat of war, which required great expenses for payment of people who were in the units but were not employed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that a lot of money came from the National Bank of Yugoslavia, and you said it's actually newly printed money. Who controlled the National Bank of Yugoslavia? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally, legally speaking, the institution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. In reality, the president of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because people from Krajina always went to the president of Serbia when it came to their needs, both financial and material needs, and that he would send those orders to the governor, prime ministers, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we go into private session for one question?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you yourself go to Mr. Milosevic for help in financing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the first occasion when did you go, and for what reason, and what was the result?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I went regarding financial matters was my third meeting with the president of Serbia. I went because of the problem that the factory called Vijak in Knin had, screw factory. Namely, the account of that factory was blocked due to a debt of 60 million dinars. This is the money they owed to the bank of Split. And I went to the president of Serbia to see if he could assist in procuring the money for the factory so that the factory could pay the debt. And on that occasion, the president of Serbia promised he would comply with this request, and later that was implemented. I think that the factory later received about 40 million in order to cover that debt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did that take place? When did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in December of 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you met him on several occasions in relation to finance. What were the other occasions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, in mid-1993, I was a member of a large delegation from the Republic of Serbia Krajina, and I was there in capacity of president of the municipality of Knin. Together with me there were prime ministers, ministers, army commanders, presidents of municipalities, and on that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. occasion we asked for greater, broader assistance from Serbia, or rather, from President Milosevic. Nikola Sainovic, Prime Minister of Serbia, attended the meeting, and he promised that all of these material and financial needs would be resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, it's about the screw factory. What factory was that, and does it have any relation to arms or something like that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you heard the question of His Honour. Can you answer that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That factory manufactured screws. In 1991, it did provide some minor services to the army, manufacturing of hand grenades, and then also material for manufacturing armoured trains. So those were minor services that were provided to the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, one more question.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to what Franko Simatovic had in Strmica. These operations were in addition to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did Mr. Milosevic ever indicate to you during a meeting that he was actually in charge of the National Bank or the Serbian administration?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This simply went without saying. That was the attitude that he had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a -- a discussion with Mr. Milosevic in April 1995 where you discussed the situation in Knin and the assistance that Knin could get?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April of 1995, I talked with President Milosevic on three occasions. In early April, I talked to him about military operations conducted by the HVO army in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the rear of Knin. On that occasion, he told me the following regarding the assistance: that it was not true that there were only 300.000 people against 4 million Croats but that there was an entire logistical support of Serbia standing behind Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, go back to the question that you asked the witness as to whether Mr. Milosevic ever indicated that he was actually in charge of the National Bank or the Serbian administration, and the witness answered: "This simply went without saying. That was the attitude that he had." I believe that requires some clarification, some amplification.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And on this -- I take this opportunity to also point out to you that in relation to these points that the witness just mentioned, there is in the summary, paragraph 95 and paragraph 267, these two paragraphs are also covered now in this section. I've pulled it together so that we do not have to repeat anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Witness, you have understood the remark of Judge Robinson. Did Mr. Milosevic -- on my question about whether he indicated to you that he was in charge of the National Bank or Serbian administration, you referred to this remark he made in relation to the 4 million -- the -- sorry, that you referred to Serbia being behind you, the Serbian system. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That meant that Krajina had enough people for combat and that all material and financial means were provided by Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your remark that it simply went without saying that Mr. Milosevic was in charge of the National Bank or the Serbian administration, what is the basis of you saying that? Why does it go without saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because any problem that was not possible to resolve with competent Ministers or the governors, that problem would be addressed to Mr. Milosevic. And after a discussion with him, that problem would later on be solved.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Witness, as the President of Serbia, Mr. Milosevic may have said that you have the full support from the Serbian people, but how is that related to the control of the bank of Yugoslavia? Could you clarify, articulate more reasons, reasons of your thinking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, President Milosevic controlled all institutions of the Republic of Serbia. And after the creation of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in April of 1992, he also controlled federal institutions of Yugoslavia. President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, which was Zoran Lilic at the time, used to describe himself as somebody who was at the disposal of President Milosevic. This is how all other institutions operated too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just mentioned President Lilic. When did he make such remarks that he was at the disposal of President Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1994, early 1995. I saw him as he left the presidential palace, Mr. Milosevic's office, and in front of me he greeted Borislav Mikelic who was then Prime Minister of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. I know that they were close, personally close. And then Mikelic asked how he was, and then he said about himself, "Well, I'm somebody who is at somebody's disposal. I'm a usable man."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to put a few more financial documents to you, and the first one is in Exhibit 352, tab -- tab 13. Sorry, tab 15. It is the request of the Minister of Finance of the RSK from the 19th of June, 1992, to the Federal Executive Council and the Federal Secretariat of Finance and the Yugoslav National Bank, and there is requested a sum of 12,900 billion dinars. And there is also mentioned that it has to go to the -- "Please pay the funds into the giro account of the budget of the Republic of Serbian Krajina." Is that the giro account in the SDK system or is it a bank account?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the budget account.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is -- looking at the letterhead and the signature, can you comment on the genuinity [sic] of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a letter sent by the Minister of Finance, the then Minister of Finance, Vojin Peuraca, who was Minister in the government of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honours, just briefly. Perhaps it's wording which is used by my learned friend. Of course the witness can comment as to the stamp that he sees, but whether he can comment as to the genuineness of the document, it's evidently a copy. But as I say, it's probably just the wording that my learned friend has used.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- you mentioned the signature. Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen this signature, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according -- and in relation to the letterhead, is that a letterhead used by the government of the RSK at that time, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a regular letterhead.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, as a reference, Mr. Morten Torkildsen has found out that the equivalent in the black market value for D-mark is approximately elf million -- 11 million, sorry. Eleven million.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is tab 13 in Exhibit 352. It's a letter of the Minister of Defence of the RSK to the ministry of -- to the Ministry of the Republic of Serbia, and it refers to a meeting held on the 12th of November, 1992, with President Milosevic and various other persons. They're all listed in paragraph 1 of this letter. When you look at the participants, Goran Hadzic, Zdravko Zecevic, Milan Martic, Stojan Spanovic, Vojin Peuraca, and Bosko Bozanic, did they have these positions at the time that they are given here in this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that such a meeting took place in November 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this meeting not take place or were you not aware of it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at the letterhead and the stamp and the signature, can you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's a stamp here of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, Belgrade office, and then Minister Spanovic here. I'm not sure about his signature, but this stamp does correspond to the stamp used at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the government of the RSK actually have such an office in Belgrade at the address given and is that the letterhead of the office?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What the stamp says does correspond to that. The government did have a representative office in Belgrade, and this is the stamp used by that office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this letter, there is, in paragraph 2 on the first page, it says: "The president, Mr. Milosevic, agreed to the concept of creating a defence system of the Krajina, which would be based on about 23.000 people Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in the police, of whom 5.000 in the regular force and 18.000 in brigades, which would make up the peacetime corps of the army and provide security for the borders in the Krajina. The view is that this number should not be reduced and that a manner and system of financing need not be found, as this number of men should remain in the standing force as the professional part of the army. It was accepted that the planning of funds for army and police needs should begin immediately, as was done in 1992 via the RSK Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia." Witness, was there such a defence concept, and was it paid in this manner described in the letter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was such a concept of defence. This concept was established in the fall of 1991 and it was financed in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the letter continues: "President Milosevic said that funds for maintaining equipment should be planned via the army of Yugoslavia, that he would help in the implementation of this, and that the army of Yugoslavia should finance the active officers and civilians who stayed behind in the Krajina. All other defence finance needs should be planned via the Ministry of Defence." Was that done in this way?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Milosevic actually agreed on this concept and endorsed it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how this system functioned. I know of some cases, for example, the appointment of the army commander. For these matters they went to see Milosevic personally. So the system did function in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, to this letter point we come a little bit later in the course of the testimony, when we go into army matters. The next document to be put to the witness is tab 17 in Exhibit 352, and it is a request from the RSK Minister of Finance to the FRY National Bank for 5 million dinars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you comment on the letterhead and the stamp and the signature?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is how the Minister of Finance communicated in those days, that is, the Minister of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, Ratko Veselinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And the next document is tab 18. It's another letter. It's the National Bank of RSK, Governor's Office, to the National Bank of Yugoslavia, in relation to the request for cash grant of 10 billion dinars of the 24th of July, 1995. Can you again comment on the letterhead, the stamp, and the signature?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the method of communication used by Pavo Marjanovic, the governor of the National Bank of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. And I also know specifically that there was this request that this letter refers to at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the request granted? Was it done that way, then?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was, because several days later the National Bank of RSK was evacuated from Knin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is tab 19 of Exhibit 352, and it's a letter of the RSK Ministry of Interior of the 5th November 1993 to the MUP of Serbia. Can you comment on the letterhead, the signature, and the stamp?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document that could have been compiled by the chief of police, that is, of public security, in the MUP of Krajina. He was Nebojsa Pavkovic, according to the stamp, but I don't know his signature. I'm not certain about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to the contents of this letter, it's actually referring to border crossing of MUP employees from Republika Srpska to the Republic of Serbia, to escort the transport of money from Belgrade to Knin. Was money transported in this manner that is indicated in this letter? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two types of cash: cash from the National Bank of Yugoslavia and cash which people from the Ministry of Interior or of the army went to fetch for themselves, to meet their own needs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "for themselves, to meet their own needs," do you mean the offices or do you mean the persons? Does that mean the offices of the army and the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the institutions: the Ministry of the Interior and the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this practice of bringing money in this manner from Serbia to the Krajina, in which time period did this operate?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was done from 1991 until 1995. In fact, in July 1995 I know that the then commander Mrksic brought money in that way for officers of the Serbian army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. He brought the money from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last document is tab 20 of that same exhibit, and it is now a letter of Milan Martic, as the Minister of Interior in Knin, to the offices of the President of the Republic of Serbia, Mr. Milosevic; the Prime Minister of the Republic of Serbia, Sainovic; and the Minister of Interior, Zoran Sokolovic, dated the 28th of April, 1993, and it's another request for funding. Can you comment on this letter, first in relation to the letterhead, the signature, and the stamp, and then in relation to the contents.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The letterhead relates to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina, the stamp of the Ministry of the Interior, and the signature, a signature that I have seen as being that of Milan Martic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware that in April 1993 additional funds were needed in this way, for the increase?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a state of armed conflict between Krajina and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Witness, we will leave now the section of finance and speak about the SAO Krajina in December 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, this I think is an area which we really can take quite quickly. You may have had that in mind. And certainly in relation to the foundation and the documents, we can go through them with very short reference indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first document I would put to you in relation to the SAO constitution and law is tab 26 in Exhibit 351, and you just need to give yes or no answers. Is this a report dated the 30th April 1991 in relation to the verification commission to verify the mandate of members of the Assembly of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina, dated on the 30th of -- yes, I said already the date. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tab 29 of that same document, and we can actually also add tab 36. Tab 29, is it the edition dated on the 30th April 1991 on the Assembly of the SAO Krajina, ratifying the election of the president of the Executive Council of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other document, is it the decision of the SAO Krajina, dated the 29th of May, 1991, proclaiming the statute of the SAO as constitutional law?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the translation is actually an error. In the English translation, it says as the date the 29th of June, 1991, but in the B/C/S it's May. The next document is tab 37 of that same document, of that same exhibit, 37.1 and 37.2. Are these the constitutional laws of the SAO Krajina of the 29th of May, 1991, and the law amending the constitutional law of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the major changes, is it actually changing the name of the Executive Council of the SAO Krajina into "government"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we have seen the other -- the original SAO statute, where there were the references to the law of Croatia and the FRY. Is there a change in this regard here? Is it now only the law of the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. There are two major changes in relation to the statute. In addition to the designation of the government of SAO Krajina, there was the constitutional establishment of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina as part of the federal territory of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next document is tab 38 in that same binder. It's a law on the government of the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is tab 40, and it's the law on the ministries of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just would like you to look at Article 6 in this document, in relation to the Ministry of Defence. It says: "The Ministry of Defence shall deal with administration matters that relate to planning and organising of defence matters concerning compulsory military service, organising and realising the civilian protection, and other matters." And in Article 7 there is the duties and the competencies of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is tab 42 in that same document, and it's the law on the courts of the SAO Krajina, and it's all dated 29th May 1991. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now the next three documents, it's tab 43, tab 52, and tab 53, again of Exhibit 351. These three documents refer -- the first one to the law on the application of regulations of the Republic of Serbia in the SAO Krajina; the next one is a decision of the government of the SAO Krajina, dated the 1st August 1991, on the application of the law on political organisations of the Republic of Serbia; and the third one is decision of the government of the SAO Krajina, dated the 1st August 1991, on the application of the law on internal affairs of the Republic of Serbia. Can you tell us why there was made a reference to the Serbian law and not the FRY law?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was no need to mention the law of the FRY. It was applied continuously. It was never abolished. So the laws of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia were implemented. As for laws which ceased to apply in Krajina and were laws of the former Socialist Republic of Croatia, and no other laws were introduced to cover the same areas for SAO Krajina, for that reason for those kinds of legislative acts it was necessary to apply the laws of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next set of documents are actually appointments of persons into positions, and I think we can even not put it to the witness. I'll just admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can read them for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And it's related to the tab 49.5, tab 49.14, tab 49.3. It's the -- it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The second binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's the second binder, and it's actually the tab 49.5, 49.8, 49.9, 49.10, 49.14, tab -- yes, that's it. I would like to ask the witness one question in private session briefly to make it clear in relation to authentication.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, during your suspect interview in Belgrade, did you provide a great deal of documents related to the SAO and the RSK and their functioning?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And most of these documents were signed by either you yourself or your colleagues in the government of these institutions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can now go into open session again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to put to the witness the exhibit tab 63 of Exhibit 351, and it is dated the 26th of October, 1991, and it is a "Decision on moving on to work in the conditions of war."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the war actually start in the SAO Krajina? Was that on that date or earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The armed conflicts were ongoing in Krajina from the middle of 1991. The real war started in August 1991 when the Yugoslav People's Army was involved on a large scale in the combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next document I would like to put to you is actually tab 59 of that same exhibit, and -- no. We can just move on. We can just move on. We don't need to discuss it. But I have a question in relation to the next document I would like to put to you, and it's tab 61 in that same document, and it is a "Decision to appoint members of the commission to establish a platform for a possible solution to the constitutional status of the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina in the future union of Yugoslav people," and it's dated the 21st of November, 1991. Can you explain why a commission was formed and what it was supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a period of time that followed the holding of the main sessions of the conference on the former Yugoslavia which was being held in The Hague. At the time, already certain changes had come into effect in the area of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and under those conditions, the SAO Krajina needed to define its own position as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And there is actually another document going with this as well. I would like to show to you the exhibit tab 62. And it's the law on internal affairs. And I have one question in relation to Article 30. Article 30 reads as follows: "The Ministry of the Interior cooperates with the organs of internal affairs in the Federation and in other republics -- and other republic and gives them help in executing tasks from their jurisdiction. "The relation and cooperation between the Ministry of Interior and the interior organs in the Federation and other republic are based on the rights and duties determined by the law..." and so on. Which other republic is referred to in Article 30?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Republic of Serbia in the first place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. This concludes the documents. I have just one question in general in relation to all these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's really absurd for a lawyer to ask who is meant in a general act which has the force of law and in which it explicitly says "cooperation with other republics," and then this poor witness answers "Republic of Serbia." Surely the law means what it says and no explanation is required. This is the law of one republic which says that its Ministry of the Interior will cooperate with other republics. It really is absurd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you will have your chance to comment on what you regard as absurdities. Let's try and get on with this evidence. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, just an additional question in relation to Article 30. With which other republics did the RSK cooperate? The SAO and the RSK, with which other republics did they cooperate?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those days with Serbia and Montenegro. There were no other republics that it could cooperate with within this context of this provision of the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to the decisions and laws that we just discussed, who drafted these decisions and laws?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boro Rasuo and Risto Matkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would also like to also very briefly address the issue of the defence law that prevailed in the SAO Krajina, and did you provide such laws during your conversations with the Prosecutor in Belgrade and in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as the Law on Defence is concerned, I provided a text which in content corresponds to the law that was applied on the 1st of August, 1991, in SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think we have to put these documents to the witness. I think just refer to them. It's a Law on All People's Defence adopted by the SFRY of 1981. That's tab 21 of Exhibit 352. Then the amending Law on People's Defence published in the Official Gazette of the SFRY in 1991. That's tab 22. Then the Serbian Law on Defence, July 1991. That's tab 24. And the next one is tab 23, the decree to enforce the Law on Defence of the Republic of Serbia in the territory of the RSK in August 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tab 25 is an additional document which I would like to discuss with you, actually, and it's tab 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could that be briefly put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a letter to the -- a letter to the president of the Municipal Assembly, informing them that the law -- in accordance with the law on the application of legal regulations of the Republic of Serbia on the territory of the SAO Krajina and who is the head of the TO, that is the Prime Minister. Is that what you supplied to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how -- how did you -- you provided -- you had available in the Krajina the Serbian Law on Defence of July 1991. How did you get it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Law on Defence of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received it from the office of the president of the Republic of Serbia, Mr. Slobodan Milosevic, by fax.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you requested it by fax, or how did it arrive?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We requested the office to send it to us by fax.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually request -- speak to Mr. Milosevic about it or did you just approach the office?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spoke to the secretary of Mr. Milosevic, asking her to ask the president whether we could have a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was it the only way to get the law of Serbia at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a way to get it quickly, without waiting for it to arrive by mail or through the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, if it's another of your comments, I think we can do without it, Mr. Milosevic. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to assist the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, no. You can assist later. We will adjourn now. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have just one question in relation to this and then it will be finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time when you requested the Serbian Law of Defence, was it already adopted or was it in the process of being adopted?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Assembly of the Republic of Serbia had adopted it, and it was in the president's office for signature, so that it was in the signature stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in the beginning of your testimony you already mentioned the Serbian media and their relevance at that time. How did the Serbian media report about the situation of the Serbs in Yugoslavia, in particular, the Serbs in Croatia, in the years 1990, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These media not only followed the events involving Serbs in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, especially in the territory of Croatia, but they worked very intensively on creating public opinion, both about the events and the general situation at the time. As political tension grew in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, and particularly the conflicts, political conflicts in Croatia in early and throughout 1990, the reporting of the media from Serbia, and especially Belgrade, was very idiosyncratic. All reports on these events were accompanied by reminiscing of events from more distant history, such as World War II, when Croatian Nazis, or the Ustashas, committed pogroms and mass crimes in the territory of the former independent state of Croatia. Generally speaking, I can say that the spectre of reporting and these evocations of historical events was led by Belgrade, in creating public opinion in the sense that mistrust was fueled against the current government in Croatia and animosity towards the new government in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was the Croatian government described?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian government was described in various ways, depending on the time period involved. It was described as neo-Ustasha government at the beginning, and at the time of the armed conflict it was also described as genocidal and Ustasha.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anything said about the intention of the Croatian government towards the Serbian population in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially in the beginning of 1990. It was said that the intention of the Croatian government was to commit a new genocide and massacres against Serbs, in Croatia especially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anything said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Especially in Knin. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anything said about the Croatian population and their relationship with Serbs? Could they live together?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The emphasis was put more on separation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Serbian media from Belgrade and Serbia report falsely about events in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say that they exaggerated events and made them more dramatic than they really were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What effect, if any, did this reporting have on the Serb population in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it had a great impact, insofar as this reporting created first mistrust and then hostility towards the Croatian government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about the Croatian population? You mentioned they had distrust and even hostility towards the Croatian government. What about the attitude towards the Croatian population?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The relationship was indirect. That is to say that it was believed that anyone who supported such a government in Croatia was the same as the government, could be identified with the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a particular media item that affected you personally?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all articles that evoked the past impressed me a great deal. There was even one interview I gave when I myself evoked that past. The reporters in question specifically asked me to. And I was particularly impressed by all the efforts to portray the intentions of the Croatian government and Croatian ministers regarding Serbs in Croatia. That is what impressed me most and inspired in me a hostility towards the Croatian authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you view the so-called Spegelj tape, Spegelj's tape? Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a film broadcast on Television Belgrade about Spegelj, Boljkovac, both ministers in the Croatian government, and their intentions regarding Serbs in Croatia, the army, and Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would like to play a few sequences of the Spegelj's tape, and it's actually Exhibit 352, tab 170. If you allow for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The AV director has the tape and knows what he has to play. Thank you. You can start.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] If it is needed, two or three men for the liquidation of the leadership.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, you have the English translation of what we hear in that same tab number. I actually thought that we would hear the translation, because I thought they were supplied with that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm told there's a problem about the interpreters following. I don't know whether they've got the translation or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: They did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you want to play some more, see how we get on?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: The quality of sound is too bad for interpreting, and we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's see how we get on with the next bit. If you can't interpret, we'll have to abandon it. Do you want to play another section? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is it still not possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It seems impossible. We have the transcript of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have the transcript now. Interpreters now have the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think we can abandon it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We've got it in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have it in English, and that should be enough. The only thing is that the witness, of course, doesn't have now the text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you review this tape in the Office of the Prosecutor while you were here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw part of that footage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Spegelj on this tape refer to killing members of the JNA, and in particular, solving the problem in Knin by slaughtering? Did he say that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who produced the video? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the film was shown, it was announced that it was produced by the information service of the Federal Secretariat for National Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Later, the media reported that the footage was actually produced by the KOS, the counter-intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Spegelj, General Spegelj at that time, did he deny to have said such things like killing the JNA members and the people in Knin?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the media he denied -- he denied this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This tape, was it -- when was it -- was it broadcast once or on several occasions and at what time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was broadcast around the 25th of January, and I know it was followed by articles in the press. It may have been broadcast several times, but I didn't watch it more than once. I watched it only the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which year was it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1991. Around the 25th of January, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this tape have an effect on the Serbian population in Croatia, in particular in Knin?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After this film, there were mass rallies not only against Spegelj but the entire Croatian government and in support of Yugoslavia and the Yugoslav People's Army. It had such an effect that the Croatian government and anyone who supported it was considered as an enemy of the Serbian people. Great fear reigned, fear of Croatia, especially at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already mentioned, actually, an interview you gave to the media, but I would like to have some additional remarks on this, but I think it should be in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put to the witness the Exhibit 352, tab 26. It's an interview that you gave in January 1991 to the Nin magazine, and it is an interview signed by Stefan Grubac. Did this man interview you, and how do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did this interview with me. And not only this one but many others in the second half of 1990 and the first half of 1991. He became very close with me. And he personally is from Drnis near Dalmatia. He became close to me in the sense that he made frequent contact with me and even made suggestions as to how I should make my public appearances and what to say. In the month of March, he asked me to write a statement on the occasion of the rallies organised by SPS during demonstrations in Belgrade. On one occasion --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we'll come to this. I actually wanted just to know how you know him. And did Mr. Gruban [sic] have contact with Mr. Milosevic? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was in contact with Mr. Milosevic's associates and close friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These persons are from the family circle of Mr. Milosevic. There is one person, a woman, from the Yugoslav left wing party and another man whose name I can't recall now. Gruban [as interpreted] also was in contact with the chief of cabinet of Mr. Milosevic. He accompanied me to his office. On one occasion, he asked me to make a statement against Vuk Draskovic, then leader of the opposition in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean Mr. Gruban [sic] had an influence on you, on what you said and when and how often?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here in this interview, actually on page 2 in the English, Mr. Gruban refers to you and says: "And to the Serb Autonomous Region of Krajina and Dr. Milan Babic, its `chancellor'...." Did he refer to you in his reports and interviews as "chancellor"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he tended to glorify me, to attach greater importance to me and my office than I really had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff, I don't think I follow you. Are we talking about "Mr. Gruban" or "Grubac"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's "Grubac."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's actually on the last page of the -- on page 7. It's "Stefan Grubac."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The transcript has been saying it as "Gruban."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sorry. It's a name you find on page 7, "Stefan Grubac."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other journalists from Serbia around you at that time glorifying you as you say?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were many journalists. I think simply that I had to, I was forced to, I was constantly asked to make statements and comment on any and every event. Especially Krste Bijelic, from the beginning of the 1990s, who was correspondent of the Radio Television Belgrade in Knin, constantly asked me for statements, and I know he bragged on one occasion that he made a politician out of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said he bragged he made a politician out of you. When did he say that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Krste Bijelic, was he related or close to Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991, he became editor of the information programme of Television Belgrade, an institution controlled by Mr. Milosevic. On one occasion even, President Milosevic told me tongue in cheek that some people are reproaching him for appointing Krste Bijelic editor of Television Belgrade through Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did he tell you that? When did Mr. Milosevic tell you that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in 1991 during one encounter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And in this interview that we just spoke about of Mr. Grubac, there is on the last page a reference that you make to the question Mr. Grubac asked you. "Serbs are being arrested these days and Croats are not. Who is engaged in `banditry' in Croatia?" And you refer in your answer to the "Croatian leadership's Ustashoid police regime." Does that mean you adopted this language that you described to us in your own speeches?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that same section, two questions down, you refer to Mr. Slobodan Milosevic, and you say that he is "...the president of all Serbs, not only of Serbia, and he enjoys the support of all Serbs." Was that so at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what he held himself out to be and promised support to Serbs, and Serbs believed him. I personally believed him too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. We can actually turn -- turn away from this document and go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I recommend that the Prosecution indicate which tabs should be under seal, in particular tab 26.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This tab should be under seal, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Mr. Milosevic -- let me ask you differently. Who controlled the Serbian media?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The media in Serbia was controlled by President Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he do that? How did he control the media? In which way?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had two options: either through the institutions of the Republic of Serbia, which he controlled through his ruling SPS party; or personally, through people which held posts of editors and media outlets. I personally know about this second option, way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about this second option, that he controlled the media through people who held posts?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he appointed and removed from office directors of radio/television; that he held, controlled, appointed, directors and editors of the daily Politika --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: To what extent was the media privately or publicly owned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was publicly owned. It was public property, ownership.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the daily Politika. Is that a leading paper? Was it a leading paper at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the leading daily, called Politika.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that Mr. Milosevic appointed the editors and those who held post in this leading paper? And if it's necessary, we can go into private session. I'm not sure yourself, but you know.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard personally, from some directors, that they were under the control of President Milosevic, and I heard personally from President Milosevic that he had appointed certain directors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did Mr. Milosevic tell you that he personally appointed directors? And who did he appoint?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March, he appointed the director of television of Belgrade, Belgrade television, in March of 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that what he told you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In March 1991, or when?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I suggest we go briefly into a private session so that the witness can speak more freely.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, which directors or editors told you personally that they were influenced or appointed by Mr. Milosevic, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. Zivorad Minovic, director of Politika, told me, in 1995, that President Milosevic knew why he held him in that office, that of director of Politika, in addition to Dragan Hadziantic, who held the office of the editor of Politika. I met Zivko Minovic for the first time at the after-elections reception, around the new year of 1991. It was a reception given by President Milosevic. And in early February 1991 I was his guest in Politika.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, when you are referring to the fact that the director said he was appointed by President Milosevic, by whom is the director supposed to be appointed, instead of Mr. Milosevic, at that time? Did Mr. Milosevic appoint him in the capacity of president legitimately, or is it different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was done differently. President of the Republic had no competence to appoint directors of media outlets. Directors were elected by the council of workers of a media outlet after there was a publicly announced vacancy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was that set out in some instrument, in a law or regulation perhaps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was regulated by various laws.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that legally it was not Mr. Milosevic who would appoint Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the editors or directors. How, then, can you say that he appointed? In which way did he take part in this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He held the power in Serbia, and through Serbia, also -- or rather, through people in Serbia, he also held power at a federal level, that of Yugoslavia. He was president of a ruling party, the party that -- or rather, he held that post for a certain amount of -- certain period of time, but practically he always held power. That party had power in the Assembly of Serbia and also in the majority of municipalities in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the party actually have a say in the decision of who becomes a director or editor?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Procedurally, it was the workers' council that decided on this. The state, or rather, the municipalities, had an insight and had supervision, so to speak, of it. This was called the so-called public supervision, social supervision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever present when Mr. Milosevic gave directions or directives to editors or directors of media, as, for instance, TV or Politika?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion, around the 23rd of January, during a meeting that I had in the office of President Milosevic, he personally went to the secretary and dictated the text of the statement and then called somebody in Politika to have it published. I can't remember what the second instance was. He said about the director of television in 1991, after the opposition in Serbia asked the then director Mitevic to resign or to be removed from office, he said, "Well, I gave him this new director." I can't remember now his new name. It's not a typical Serb last name. But he said his name and then said, "His father was a member of the Ljotic units, and now they basically have no reason to oppose him."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the editors tell you that they got directives from Mr. Milosevic personally?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have contact with Mr. Rade Brajevic, and can you tell us who that is?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Brajevic was editor of Vecernje Novosti, a daily. I met him on a number of occasions, starting in 1990, both in Knin and in the offices of Vecernje Novosti, and in the cabinet of President Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The daily Novosti, is that a widely published state newspaper, a publicly owned publishing house?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was publicly owned, but I'm not quite sure who was the founder of Vecernje Novosti. It could have been the enterprise Borba, which was a federal institution, but it also could have been founded by somebody else. And they had a more independent policy than Borba. Now, as to their exact status and their founder, I'm not quite sure, but they were publicly owned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a conversation with Mr. Rade ^ Brajevic in relation to an interview that you gave in 1994 that was then not published?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we met -- after meeting him in President Milosevic's cabinet, he asked me to be his guest and to have his journalists conduct an interview with me. I was their guest, but the interview was done separately from that time when I was their guest, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness, we're not really getting very far with all this. Shall we move on, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. We can go into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back into open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the media also report about Milan Martic, and if so, in which way?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They did write about him, especially starting in April of 1991.
